text: A filter that claims to address collapse must beat real-data retention, not only unfiltered replacement, because retaining ten percent of the original data slows the damage.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518

isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: The comparator standard follows from published results on real-data retention.
It sets a requirement on what a filter must show, not a result about any filter.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: Retaining ten percent of the original data slows the damage (Shumailov et al. 2024), and accumulating all real data keeps test error bounded in the settings studied (Gerstgrasser et al. 2024; Kazdan et al. 2025), although even a synthetic share as small as 1 per 1,000 can stop larger training sets from helping in regression (Dohmatob et al. 2025). A filter that claims to address collapse must therefore beat real-data retention, not only unfiltered replacement.
